correctness.rationale: Cycle transfer formula and the signed merge identity are proved algebraically; nine explicitly listed local coefficientwise comparisons produce monotone terminating replacements for every cycle partition; independent-set event translates to coextinction avoidance. originality.rationale: In inspected published literature, the whole coefficientwise cycle-partition extremal theorem (including both residue families and both loss protocols) is not covered. Zhao and Sah et al. partly cover only divisible-order pointwise fugacity extremizers; Alexander-Mink prove limited fixed-cardinality cases; ecological sources do not address these cycle partitions. Earlier local coextinction moments do not imply full zero-event probabilities. Historical priority remains provisional and database absence alone is not treated as proof.
residual_risks: An older exact independence-polynomial cycle-replacement result may exist under another title or terminology.
General graph-polynomial theorems with coefficientwise conclusions were not shown to subsume the exact residual extrema; broader unindexed work requires independent check.
This does not claim novel divisible-order scalar-fugacity extremal values already covered by Zhao and Sah et al.

value.rationale: Probability of avoiding any secondary extinction is a directly meaningful whole-network robustness functional. The theorem gives exact, fully described universal optimizers for all numbers of lost patches and all iid deletion probabilities, even at order residues not covered by simple all-C3 or all-C4 constructions. This is a structural classification, not merely a fixed-n numerical table.
